=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_noop_suspicious_recovery.py:113-124 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The contract test `test_standalone_snapshot_batches_clean_prs_and_skips_draft_claude_reads` searches for bare `if [ ` guards. The production code in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (LAST RUN DIFF hunk at lines 25026-25038 and 25223-25236) now guards on `if [[ "${S_HEAD_OID}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] && [ "${_STANDALONE_CLEAN_PRS["${S_PR}"]:-}" = "${S_HEAD_OID}" ]; then` and the analogous `_STANDALONE_NOOP_CLEAR_PRS` form. The exact substring `if [ "${_STANDALONE_CLEAN_PRS["${S_PR}"]:-}"` is NOT present because the line begins with `if [[ ... ]] &&`. `text.index(...)` raises `ValueError: substring not found`.
  WHY: CI run 37496485410 logs `ERROR test_standalone_snapshot_batches_clean_prs_and_skips_draft_claude_reads: ValueError: substring not found` on `orchestrate-poll (0)` and `orchestrate-poll (3)`. The direct-runner only catches `AssertionError`, so the `ValueError` propagates and the test module exits non-zero. The substring assertions were not updated when the SHA binding was introduced to the production code (a behavior the previous autofix claimed to "bind … and update the behavioral test" but only updated `test_standalone_batch_accepts_matching_sha_and_falls_back_on_uncertainty`, not this snapshot test). Suggested minimal fix: drop the leading `if [` prefix from both `conflict.index(...)` and `noop.index(...)` assertions so they search for `${_STANDALONE_CLEAN_PRS["${S_PR}"]:-}"` and `${_STANDALONE_NOOP_CLEAR_PRS["${N_PR}"]:-}"` respectively — those substrings still uniquely appear inside the SHA-guarded `if`.
- tests/test_orchestrator_judges_claude_engine.py:~220-252 (test_combined_rb_judge_uses_verified_engine_and_its_worktree) | severity=critical | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test extracts a bash code chunk from `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` using two whitespace-sensitive split markers, then runs it through `bash -c` with a fake `ai_engine.sh`. The verdict file is empty. Both parametrized cases (`issue_labels="ai:orchestrator-managed","ai:codex"` and `issue_labels="ai:done"`) fail.
  WHY: CI run 37496485410 logs `AssertionError: assert '' == 'opencode verdict\n'` on `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`. The PR added `replay_failed_reclarify_commands()` plus its `RECLARIFY_REQUEUE_SWEEP_ONLY` early-exit block near the top of the file (LAST RUN DIFF hunk at lines 19-94). The test fixture reads `POLLER.read_text()` and slices for `RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_LABELS_JSON=`; the actual `RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_LABELS_JSON=…` block is several thousand lines later in the file. If the in-between lines contain text that interferes with the parser (e.g. the new top-of-file function introduces comments or strings that match one of the split markers, or the `RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_LABELS_JSON=` text shifted out of the parser's reach), the extracted `branch` text is empty or truncated and the `RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_LABELS_JSON=…` env assignment becomes a no-op, leaving `RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_RC` unset and the verdict unwritten. Suggested minimal fix: re-run the test to confirm; if reproducible, use the live orchestrator-judge branch to extract the block with `re.search(r'^\s*RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_LABELS_JSON=(.*?)\n\s*if \[\[ "\${RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_RC}" -eq 77 \]\]', text, re.S)` (or relax the leading-whitespace match) so the new top-of-file content cannot break extraction.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:test_state_identity_failure_skips_reconstruction_and_state_writes (test file not in LAST RUN CHANGED FILES; reads from POLLER) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test fails on `orchestrate-poll (3)` shard of run 37496485410 with the truncated log line `FAIL test_state_identity_failure_skips_reconstruction_and_state_writes:` (no further detail). The PR added a 70+ line `replay_failed_reclarify_commands()` function and an early `if [ "${RECLARIFY_REQUEUE_SWEEP_ONLY:-false}" = "true" ]; then … exit 0` branch near the top of `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (LAST RUN DIFF at lines 19-94, well before the poller's main state-machine body the test exercises).
  WHY: The new top-of-file code may shift line numbers or introduce identifiers (`replay_failed_reclarify_commands`, `RECLARIFY_REQUEUE_SWEEP_ONLY`) that the test fixture's mocked environment intercepts unexpectedly, or the early-exit branch breaks a sourced-helper assumption when the test sources the script. Without seeing the test source I cannot pinpoint the exact trigger, but the failure is real and CI-confirmed and only reproducible against the PR head.
